note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Attention-derived dependencies motivate AGDO training and its results

nodes.name: Random masking mismatches inference
nodes.description: Existing dLLM post-training randomly masks tokens and optimizes the masked positions, which does not match the actual inference dynamics of dLLMs and causes a training-inference mismatch.

nodes.name: Fixed orders ignore emergent dependencies
nodes.description: Blockwise SFT and left-to-right masking impose externally defined decoding orders, although under bidirectional attention token dependencies emerge dynamically rather than following positional order.

nodes.name: Attention is sparse and temporally stable
nodes.description: In dLLMs (Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, MATH-500 queries, final layer) attention is sparse, with diagonal self/neighbour patterns and a few hub columns, and each token attends to largely the same context tokens across denoising steps.

nodes.name: Valid attention predicts stability
nodes.description: Tokens that allocate more attention to already-unmasked tokens (higher valid attention score S) show greater probability stability, i.e. smaller probability drops during later denoising, showing a positive S-vs-delta-P correlation.

nodes.name: Attention-aware selection improves accuracy
nodes.description: Choosing among masked tokens with probability above 0.9 the one with highest S beats the max-probability baseline on MATH-500 at lengths 128/256/512 (21.2 vs 16.8, 16.2 vs 13.8, 15.2 vs 13.0).

nodes.name: Attention-guided denoising order
nodes.description: AGDO derives a denoising order by starting from prompt tokens as unmasked, repeatedly selecting the top-n tokens by valid attention score S and recomputing S, so tokens are denoised only after attention-supported context exists.

nodes.name: Hub-token influence score
nodes.description: The influence score I_k of a token is the total final-layer attention it receives from other tokens, and high-I tokens act as attention hubs with disproportionate influence on generation.

nodes.name: AGDO-SFT
nodes.description: AGDO-SFT masks only the tokens assigned to each denoising step along the attention-guided order and weights the cross-entropy loss by (1 + gamma*I_k).

nodes.name: AGDO-RL
nodes.description: AGDO-RL applies the attention-guided order within GRPO and adjusts the advantage as A' = A + sign(A)*delta*I, amplifying updates for attention-central tokens.

nodes.name: AGDO-SFT beats SFT baselines
nodes.description: On Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, AGDO-SFT averages 36.0% versus 34.4% for blockwise SFT, with a 3.0% gain on Minerva.

nodes.name: AGDO-RL sets new state of the art
nodes.description: AGDO-RL outperforms RL baselines, e.g. 18.3% on LiveBench versus 15.2% for diffu-GRPO, with more sustained and stable accuracy growth during training.

nodes.name: Order alone helps
nodes.description: With gamma=0 (no influence weighting) AGDO-SFT still beats blockwise SFT by about 2% on MATH500, isolating the benefit of the attention-guided denoising order; gamma=100 gives the best result.

nodes.name: Generalizes to LLaDA
nodes.description: On LLaDA-8B-Instruct (GSM8K, MATH500) AGDO outperforms d1-LLaDA, wd1 and LLaDA1.5 and improves faster than Diff-GRPO.

isolated_nodes.name: RL on dLLMs lacks factorization
isolated_nodes.description: dLLMs do not admit a sequential token factorization, complicating the likelihood ratios and KL terms needed for GRPO; prior work uses mean-field approximations.

isolated_nodes.name: AGDO-RL strong across block sizes
isolated_nodes.description: AGDO-RL gets the highest average accuracy of 51.6% across block sizes, peaking at 53.7% with block size 64.

structural_reasoning: Prior-method limitations and the attention analysis motivate the denoising order; the order plus influence scores define SFT and RL variants whose results and ablations follow.
